reason: Steel can provide a rigid foundation for a crossing over the soft wash.
expectation: The steel will form or support a crossing over the soft ground.

alternatives.reason: The mesh and steel might first need to be assembled into a crossing surface.

effect: Steel cannot be used directly at the crossing; its listed partner is cargo mesh.
reaction: The failed attempt clarified that the crossing needs an intermediate assembly.
reason: Steel and cargo mesh are confirmed partners and may form the supported crossing surface.
expectation: They will make a rigid, reinforced crossing surface.

effect: The steel and mesh made stiffened traction panels suitable for distributing wheel loads.
reaction: The physical explanation makes the intermediate assembly clear.
reason: The framed panels appear suited to supporting the rover across the soft wash.
expectation: The panels will be laid across the soft section to support the rover's wheels.

effect: The panels now support the crossing, and the next goal is to get the rover across.
reaction: The explanation of how the rails spread the load is satisfying.
reason: The winch and sound rock anchor suggest a secure way to assist the rover across.
expectation: The winch will be secured to the rock to help the rover cross the supported panels.

effect: The winch is anchored to sound rock, ready to assist the crossing.
reaction: The aligned pull gives the recovery setup a clear purpose.
reason: The anchored winch and supported panels are the two preparations for taking the rover across.
expectation: The rover will cross the panels with assistance from the anchored winch.

effect: The anchored winch and supported panels got the rover across, completing the chapter; the same route remains available for the return.
reaction: The controlled crossing was a satisfying payoff for the two preparations.

mostWorthwhile.text: Building and laying the framed traction panels was most worthwhile: the explanation made clear why stiff rails spread wheel loads better than loose mesh.

leastWorthwhile.text: Trying steel directly at the crossing was a small unproductive detour, though the feedback identified its partner.

surprise.text: I initially expected steel to support the crossing directly; the game instead required it to be assembled with mesh into framed panels.

arbitrary.text: The final combination of winch and panels is an abstraction of driving the rover, but the resulting description makes its purpose clear. Nothing felt strongly arbitrary.

continue.text: Yes. The physically explained preparations were satisfying, and I would like to see what the expedition finds at the exposed ice.
